messages:
maya: quick note — a user hit a weird TS inference/overload problem in the quickstart when deploying to Vercel Edge. works in node, fails in the edge bundle. they see `any`/`unknown` leak after calling `client.call({ model, parse })`.

ash: ugh that pattern again. do we still ship overloads for call()?

maya: yes, simplified: `call(opts: {model:string}):Promise<string>` and `call<T>(opts:{model:string; parse:(s:string)=>T}):Promise<T>`. node picks up the CJS d.ts, edge picks ESM d.ts and the overload order/resolution differs.

pete: bundler + `type:module` consumers often hit that. easiest fixes: collapse to single generic with `T = unknown` or add the generic overload first so inference prefers it.

ash: also check package.json exports: if import entry doesn't include `types` pointing at the ESM d.ts, consumers may get the wrong .d.ts. adding \"types\": \"./dist/esm/index.d.ts\" under the import export helped us before.

maya: agreed. user had `module:ES2022` + `moduleResolution: bundler` in their tsconfig (Vite default) which seems to be the trigger.

pete: short term: 1) update quickstart tsconfig note (don't rely on skipLibCheck), 2) ship a single-generic public signature, 3) publish per-entry types in exports.

infra-bot: CI / quickstart-typecheck failed on branch fix/edge-types (log: https://ci.redwood/edge/456) :x:

ash: i'll open a tiny PR that replaces the overloads with `export function call<T = string>(opts: { model: string; parse?: (s: string)=>T }): Promise<T>;` and add `types` on the import entry. i'll also add a tsc job to CI using `moduleResolution: \"bundler\" + module: \"ES2022\"` to catch regressions.

maya: please also include a minimal repro repo in the PR so folks can run local Vite/esbuild builds. users consistently get frustrated by this during onboarding.

pete: long-term: we should standardize our emitted d.ts shape between CJS/ESM builds (declarationMap + identical re-export ordering) so resolver doesn't flip overload selection. also consider documenting conditional typing patterns for advanced users.

maya: cool — will track in the PR. thanks all. :wave:
